title: Fuel-analysis specification
text: This is a pre-analysis specification for publication development. It records the existing pipeline and proposed decisions; it does not modify data or generate publication results.

title: Fuel-analysis specification
section: Existing thesis-era handling to preserve as a reference
text:
Existing thesis-era handling to preserve as a reference
analysis/analysis/fuel_modeling_round_3.qmd labels and models 1-hour, 10-hour, 100-hour, 1,000-hour, duff-and-litter, vegetation, and vegetation difference classes. Duff and litter are combined as dufflitter. The post-precommercial-thinning workflow excludes dufflitter because the existing script notes that the collected litter-depth information is not suitable for its load equation. The workflow also converts nonpositive veg_diff values to zero before fitting the post-treatment models.
These choices define the historical thesis analysis. They must remain reproducible and must not be overwritten.

title: Fuel-analysis specification
section: Publication decisions to make before coding
text:
Publication decisions to make before coding

Identify exactly which raw measurement fields can support separate reporting of duff, litter, live vegetation, and each dead-fuel time-lag class at each measurement phase.
Decide whether the publication’s primary fuel product is modeled treatment estimates, descriptive/reference summaries, or both. The current direction favors reference summaries, with treatment comparisons retained only when they aid interpretation.
Specify how pre- and post-precommercial-thinning observations will be presented: as distinct reference phases, a paired change analysis, or both.
Define how zero values, missing values, and any negative derived differences will be handled, including sensitivity checks where that choice could affect interpretation.
Select a small set of units, component definitions, and uncertainty measures suitable for reuse in future fire-modeling studies.

title: Fuel-analysis specification
text:
Required publication outputs

A data dictionary for each published fuel component and its units.
A reproducible publication-specific derived dataset in analysis/outputs/publication/data/.
A written model or summary specification in analysis/scripts/publication/.
Main-text reference figures/tables and supplemental detail, both stored under analysis/outputs/publication/.
A comparison note describing any material difference between thesis-era and publication-era component definitions or estimates.

title: Fuel-analysis specification
text:
Guardrails

Do not modify analysis/analysis/fuel_modeling_round_3.qmd or overwrite analysis/fuel_modeling_round_3.rda.
Do not alter raw data in data/.
Record analytical changes in publication/editorial-log.qmd before they are used in manuscript text.

title: Main-text figure and table plan
text:
Supplementary displays
The supplement is the default location for the current detailed model listings, dispersion/hurdle specifications, full pairwise-comparison tables, Douglas-fir detail, secondary sprout figures, and expanded pre/post fuel comparisons. This preserves reproducibility without requiring each item to carry the main silvicultural narrative.

title: Publication manuscript development
text:
This standalone Quarto project is the publication-development workspace for the Redwood Multiaged Experiment. It is intentionally separate from the legacy profile-driven project in analysis/.
The manuscript will retain the thesis as its substantive starting point while being reorganized around a regeneration-first pyro-silviculture narrative. Fuel conditions will be reported as disaggregated reference values that can support future fire-modeling work.

title: Publication manuscript development
text:
Working boundaries
This project does not execute or alter the thesis-era analyses. Future publication-specific derived data, model objects, figures, and tables will be written to ../analysis/outputs/publication/. Shared raw data, utilities, figures, and bibliography resources remain in their established repository locations until a stable shared interface is deliberately extracted.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Forest managers using retention forestry need information on regeneration and fuel development to design productive stands in fire-adapted ecosystems. We analyzed 10-year remeasurement data from the Redwood Multiaged Experiment in Jackson Demonstration State Forest, California. The experiment compared group selection, aggregated retention, and low- and high-density dispersed retention treatments and measured regeneration, sprout growth, and surface fuel loading.
Redwood regeneration responded strongly to increasing canopy openness, whereas tanoak responses were more modest. Fuel measurements describe conditions before and after precommercial thinning and provide reference values for future fire and fuels modeling in these redwood systems. The manuscript will evaluate how overstory retention affects regeneration while presenting fuel components in a form useful for integrated silviculture and fire management.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Study area and design
The experiment is located in the Jackson Demonstration State Forest in coastal northern California. Four harvest treatments were replicated at four sites in 2012: group selection (GS), high-density dispersed retention (HD), high-density aggregated retention (HA), and low-density dispersed retention (LD). The retained-overstory treatments targeted post-harvest relative densities of 13% or 21%; group selection created a 1-ha opening with a lightly thinned buffer. These treatments were designed to examine alternative pathways for developing multiaged redwood stands (Berrill & O’Hara, 2009; Reineke, 1933).
Ten years after harvest, regeneration plots and fuel transects were established within each 0.2-ha treatment macro plot. Regeneration measurements characterized redwood, tanoak, and Douglas-fir; fuel transects characterized dead surface fuels and live vegetation. The plots were remeasured after precommercial thinning, which released selected conifers from competing trees and shrubs.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Analysis
The final publication methods will identify the regeneration models retained from the thesis and the revised fuel-component specifications separately. Detailed sampling procedures, model diagnostics, and expanded comparisons will be retained as supplementary material where they are needed for reproducibility but not for interpretation of the main findings.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Regeneration under varying overstory retention
The thesis results provide the starting material for basal area, Douglas-fir occurrence, and sprout-height summaries. At 10 years after harvest, redwood regeneration was greatest in the most open treatment and declined with greater overstory retention. Tanoak responses were comparatively modest, and Douglas-fir regeneration was less frequent. The final figures and summaries will retain these results only after the publication presentation and modeling review are complete.

title: Regeneration and fuel loading with varying overstory retention in redwood stands
text:
Fuel conditions as reference values
Fuel conditions are reported second to support interpretation of the silvicultural treatments and to provide reference values for subsequent fire and fuels studies. The thesis found comparatively few treatment differences in fine dead fuels before precommercial thinning, whereas vegetation fuels were greater in more open treatments. The publication analysis will separate fuel components that were previously combined and will limit treatment-comparison emphasis to findings that aid interpretation.

title: Section compression map
text: This map defines editorial choices for the thesis-derived publication draft. The classifications are provisional and do not remove material from the thesis.

title: Section compression map
text:
Page-budget working guide
The current target is a manuscript of approximately 30 or more double-spaced pages including main-text figures and tables. Until journal requirements are applied, use this planning allocation: introduction 4–5 pages; methods 4–5; results 7–9 including displays; discussion and conclusions 6–8; references and front matter 4–6. Supplementary material is outside this working allocation.
